Hi Ava / Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft the SOW: 

What we heard
- HelixBio prefers a Private on-prem, air-gapped deployment for inference workloads (control plane isolated).
- Helix intends to manage physical site security and network perimeter; Redwood will provide the inference appliance + software image.
- Compliance requirement: quarterly firmware/OS patching, signed patch logs retained for 3 years.
- Access model: limited vendor access via escort/visitor credentials; no persistent external network access to inference hosts.

Open items we need from you
1) Site diagram (rack layout, DMZ/network demarcation) — helps size network zoning for management plane.
2) Credentialing process: how we request on-site engineer access, who signs escort requests, badge/ID process and LOA if required.
3) Confirmation of patch window preferred cadence and blackout dates for experiments.
4) Spare-parts SLA / vendor delivery constraints (lead times).

Redwood proposed next steps
- Please send site diagram + any existing BOM or hardware constraints (we can provide a reference BOM).
- Internal: Ben to propose a hardware BOM and Marissa to draft an offline patch MOP and rollback plan.
- Schedule a 30-min technical survey (onsite or remote video walk) week of Jan 26 — does Jan 27 or 28 work?

Attachments we will prepare: reference BOM, sample MOP for offline patching, and an example signed-image workflow. If you can confirm the three items above, we’ll include them in the SOW draft.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Jasmine / team —

Draft BOM and offline strategy below. I attached a spreadsheet (redwood_onprem_bom_v2.xlsx) with unit SKUs and lead-time notes. High-level summary: 

Recommended initial configuration (2-rack starter):
- 2 x compute racks, each with: 1 x 2U inference chassis (supports 4x SXM GPUs), 4 x SXM GPU slots populated with NVIDIA A40/A100 80GB class GPUs (or equivalent), 8 x 3.84TB NVMe for model store + scratch, redundant power (2x PDUs), 10Gb management + 100Gb data fabric per rack.
- Management console: OOB KVM-over-IP localized to management VLAN; if fully air-gapped, we recommend a removable KVM console that can be physically attached during maintenance windows.
- Spare parts: 1x spare GPU, 2x spare NVMe, 1x spare PDU, spare CPU/motherboard kit.

Offline patch & signed-image approach
- We can produce cryptographically-signed images (SHA256 + time-stamped signature). Helix can verify the signature before applying. We recommend a three-stage rollout for firmware/OS updates in air-gapped sites:
  1) Canary node (1 GPU node) 
  2) Pilot rack (1 full rack) after 24-48h validation
  3) Full roll (remaining racks) after successful pilot validation

- Patch window recommendation: 4–6 hours per rack for firmware + OS; allow 24–48h for validation after pilot. If Helix requires physical-only updates, we can provide signed images and a step-by-step verification checklist: image hash verification, image signing key metadata, and an expected-downtime checklist.

- Logistics: typical lead times for GPUs and chassis are 6–10 weeks (depending on distro); spares inventory should be pre-staged where possible. For critical sites, we recommend a one-week local inventory buffer for essential spares.

I attached the BOM with part numbers and lead-time columns. Let me know if you want a conservative vs cost-optimized SKU list.
